changes.after: Props give a component the information it needs to show.

before: Props are inputs passed to a component. Two uses of the same component can receive different values. Treat props as read-only: the component describes a result from its inputs rather than changing those inputs.

Define Pass to display its name prop. Render passes for Cedar and Fern in App; the same component must also display another supplied name. The starter is the small application to edit; the examples above remain available for comparison.
after: A prop is an input passed to a component. The component receives its props in an object. Read those inputs without changing them.
`props.name` reads the name supplied to that use of `Pass`. Changing only the second name changes only the second paragraph. The component does not need a new definition.
Make `Pass` show its `name` prop. In `App`, use it for `Cedar` and `Fern`. It should also work when given a different name.

after: Show the supplied prop instead of writing a fixed name inside Pass.

before.question: App uses <Pass name="Oak" /> twice. How many paragraphs does this produce?
choices: One paragraph because the function has one definition
Two paragraphs that share and overwrite one name
before.explanation: Each JSX use asks React for its own component result, even when the prop values are equal.

after.question: App uses `<Pass name="Oak" />` twice. What appears?
choices: One paragraph, because Pass is defined once.
Two paragraphs that overwrite one shared name.
after.explanation: Each use of Pass produces its own paragraph, even when the names match.

project.title: Props configure separate component uses
project.task: Make Pass show its name prop. Use it for Cedar and Fern in App.
